name: Atlantic Health
title: Why doctors weren't referring
tagline: Message testing for a $65M proton therapy center — finding the words that doubled physician referral intent.

intro: Atlantic Health invested $65 million in a state-of-the-art upright proton therapy center — technology that treats cancer with submillimeter precision while patients sit upright. But the physicians who would refer patients weren't referring.

I led qualitative and quantitative research to understand why, then developed and tested the messaging strategy that fixed it. The final framework was adopted across physician-facing email campaigns, landing pages, and future advertising.

sections.label: Executive summary
sections.heading: Physicians didn't understand why upright treatment mattered clinically
body: The center's early messaging led with innovation and patient comfort. Physicians heard it — and filed upright positioning away as a comfort feature rather than a clinical advantage. Comfort doesn't drive referrals; clinical outcomes do.
The strategic shift: stop selling leadership and comfort, and directly connect upright positioning to measurable clinical outcomes — precision, reduced motion, protected healthy tissue.

sections.label: Phase 01
sections.heading: Qualitative interviews: locating the gap
body: Goal: understand how physicians interpreted the proton therapy system, to sharpen the quantitative survey before testing nationally.

I needed to understand how physicians currently evaluated proton therapy providers, what made messaging feel clinically credible, and whether they understood the clinical value of upright positioning — in order to define referral decision-making patterns, trust drivers and skepticism triggers, reactions to early messaging concepts, and gaps in understanding around upright treatment.

quote.text: Physicians understood upright positioning as a comfort feature rather than a clinical advantage.
quote.attr: The insight that shaped the entire messaging strategy

sections.label: Phase 02
sections.heading: Quantitative message testing: 15+ messages, four dimensions
body: I developed and tested more than fifteen messages, first refined through the qualitative findings, then measured nationally on clarity, credibility, differentiation, and referral impact.
Updated messaging outperformed broad leadership language across all measured dimensions. The pattern was consistent: specificity won. Numbers beat adjectives; mechanisms beat mission statements.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.heading: The words are part of the product
body: A $65M facility with best-in-class technology was invisible to its audience because of a framing error — comfort versus clinical value. Research found the gap, testing proved the fix, and referral intent doubled without changing anything about the product itself.
It's the same lesson I keep re-learning across brand and product work: before you redesign the thing, check whether people understand what the thing is.
